relevance_note: Case report of two boys with HLH and TNFAIP3 variants ("Herein, we report two children with the primary presentation of HLH, with a mutation in TNFAIP3, in favor of HA20."), plus a literature table (Table 3) of two earlier HLH/MAS patients and three earlier HA20 patients described in the Discussion.
method_note: Built by hand-written Python (no table transcription by script); every span checked verbatim by script. Labels: the two first-hand patients are labelled by their section headings 'Patient one' and 'Patient two' (they also appear as 'Our patient N. 1/N. 2' in Table 3 and as 'our first/second patient' in text). Table 3 (literature table) has a bare-number column 'Number', so the two prior patients are 'Table 3 #1' (Li et al, also described in text with ref [29]) and 'Table 3 #2' (Takagi et al, ref [9]); Table 3 rows 3-4 are Patient one/two, not separate people. The three patients of Zhang et al. [25] are included under the v4 passing-mention rule because individual features are given; the paper does not explicitly state their TNFAIP3 status or HA20 diagnosis (implied by context and the cited title), so they have no variant rows and disease_label is 'not reported'. The other three HA20 patients of Li et al. are mentioned only as a count and get no rows. Patient two's parents are in scope as tested-negative relatives ('his parents are homozygous wild type'); sex not stated, labelled 'parent of Patient two' and 'parent of Patient two 2'. Patient one's healthy, untested older sister and untested parents get no rows. is_proband left null for both index patients: the paper has two patients and never uses 'proband' or 'index case'. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) Patient two's protein change is printed 'p. L275P' but described in words as 'a proline to leucine amino acid change' (L275P denotes leucine to proline); recorded as printed. (2) Patient one: text says 'He had normal ESR, CRP, and procalcitonin levels', but Table 1 lists ESR 11 (range 0-10), CRP 6 (range <6) and procalcitonin 0.2 (range <0.1), none asterisked; recorded as excluded from the text with the table values in severity_or_detail, checklist inflammatory markers 'excluded' - a reviewer may prefer 'not reported'. (3) Table 1 ALP 1328 (range 180-1200) is not asterisked though text says ALP mildly elevated (no conflict in direction). (4) Li et al patient's variant is 'c.C259T, p.R87X' in Table 3 and 'c.259C > T (p.R87X)' (RS: NM_006290) in text; one variant row using the text form, both spans given. (5) Patient two coagulation profile described as 'normal, except for thrombocytopenia' while fibrinogen was low; no coagulopathy row emitted. Takagi patient: text says 'de novo mutation of TNFAIP3 was detected' without stated parental testing, so inheritance is 'not reported' (rule 8). Patient one's zygosity, variant type and inheritance are not stated for his variant; only general statements ('Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in A20 cause HA20') exist, which do not count (D-29). In-silico predictions (CADD 29.1, SIFT/PolyPhen-2 'probably deleterious') for Patient two are not functional assays and not the authors' classification, so functional_evidence and pathogenicity are 'not reported'. Normal whole investigations not given feature rows: Patient one vital signs, echocardiography, urine/stool exam and cultures; Patient two metabolic evaluation, BCG scar and tonsils. Group statements naming 'our patients'/'Both of our patients' (MAS criteria, no autoantibodies, no Behcet's-like/autoimmune symptoms) were applied to both first-hand patients as 'inferred from group statement'; the broad 'no Behcet's-like symptoms' statement was not used to exclude narrower checklist items. Checklist judgment calls: 'intermittent fever' mapped to recurrent fever observed (Patient one, ref [25] patients 1 and 3); Patient one's cerebral hemorrhage mapped to CNS involvement observed; HLH cytopenias not counted as autoimmune cytopenia; Takagi's ALPS diagnosis not counted as lymphoproliferation beyond the table's 'lymphadenopathy'. Table 3 '-' in 'Other features' for our patients is undefined, so treated as not reported.
